steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until crisp, about 10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate, reserving about 1 tablespoon of the bacon drippings. Crumble the bacon once cool to the touch.
Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source.

Heat the reserved bacon drippings in a separate skillet over medium heat. Stir the butter and garlic salt into the bacon drippings; allow the butter to melt completely. Cook the scallops in the butter mixture until there is a light brown coating on each side, about 4 minutes per side. Transfer the scallops to a baking dish. Spoon the butter sauce over the scallops. Drizzle the horseradish sauce over the scallops and sprinkle with the crumbled bacon.
Bake the scallops under the preheated broiler until the sauce begins to bubble, about 1 minute.

review.reviewBody: This was really delicious!! I was not sure about the combination of flavors in this dish, but everything worked very well together and it was very easy. Other reviewers were right about it being salty-the next time I make it, I will lower the amount of garlic salt and add garlic powder to replace it because I think the bacon grease adds a key flavor component to the dish. Also, because I did not have horseradish sauce, I mixed up my own with horseradish, mayo, a touch of vinegar and pepper (you could make it with sour cream too, but I have a dairy issue). One other thing that I did was streamline in terms of pans used. I cooked the bacon in the microwave, then poured off the drippings. Also, I used a broiler safe skillet, and rather than move everything to a baking dish, I just added the final ingredients to the pan and put it under the broiler. It tasted amazing and dirtied fewer dishes! We will definitely be making this again-thank you so much for the recipe!!

Fantastic recipe. Made it twice in one week because at the request of the men in my family. I didn't have garlic salt, so I used garlic powder and kosher salt which I had in the pantry. Served over sauteed spinach as pictured. Since the scallops cook so quickly, I made the spinach first, kept it warm on my serving platter is a slightly warm oven; less than 10 minutes later, scallops were ready to place on top of spinach...then dinner time...mmm...mmmm! Recipe was so easy...so quick...and so good. Thank you.

This was wonderful. I used to cast-iron skillet to sear so there was no reason to transfer to casserole dish to broil. Just went straight to the broiler. It's like scallops wrapped in bacon without all the work. We definitely make again.

OMG the best yet. For those who said it was to salty the way to change that is use unsalted butter and fresh minced garlic. If they were not so expensive in my neck of the woods would make them every night!! I used huge scallops and quartered them but at 20 bucks a pound only used a half pond:-)

I made some fairly decent adjustments to this recipe after reading reviews about the saltiness (and because i was lacking some ingredients), but my final product came out fantastic. First, I used pancetta instead of bacon. Second, I used about two cloves of fresh garlic instead of garlic salt. Third, I used red pepper flake,and added it in when I sautéed the garlic, in place of the horseradish. I think those flavors melded really well and gave the scallops more of an Italian flair. I served them over basmati (or jasmine?) rice and they tasted great. I could also image they would be really tasty served over pasta.

Special restaurant quality! Thanks so much for this recipe, it is permanent in my recipe favorites. I apologize for slight modifications, it was perfect as written! I happened to have some homemade creme fraiche (Chef John’s, this site) so I made the homemade horseradish sauce (also Chef John’s, this site) and that was a very good decision. I also used fresh minced garlic rather than garlic salt, thinking the bacon would add all the salt needed, also good decision.

Oh my. So delicious! I used Chef John's recipe for homemade horseradish sauce rather than store bought.. that was awesome too. I used fresh garlic rather than garlic powder and left out all salt except what naturally occurring in bacon. I took a tip from others and used 3 slices bacon for a lb of scallops. Will definitely be making this again

Amazing! Favorite way to do scallops! Used bacon left over from breakfast and used 2 cloves fresh garlic instead of garlic salt. Since I used salted butter and bacon didn't add any other salt. Added green onions to top and it's a favorite of ours now! And ready in just minutes!

These were amazing! Beacause of other reviewers saying it was a little too salty, I didn't add the bacon drippings. I did use 8 pieces of bacon instead of five. I made my own horseradish sauce with mayo, sour cream and bottled horseradish. If you like scallops you will love this easy recipe!!

I made this as detailed except did not use any garlic. I added a couple tablespoons of sour cream to the horseradish and drizzled before broiling. NO added salt needed. I used organic uncured bacon. Father's Day dinner with a fresh pineapple /raisin coldslaw with ginger mandarin dressing and wild rice. It was a hit.

I would just change the garlic salt content. It was too salty, so I'd have a third of the original amount because the bacon is salty, and the horseradish adds another element of salty/sour/spicy that made it a bit overwhelming. Otherwise great recipe for scallops.
I followed the suggestions of others completely omitting the garlic salt and It was delicious! Served with some pasta on the side and served the sauce with the scallops on top.
Not a good flavor combo for tender tasty scallops, would be great on steak or a baked potato but not $18/fresh scallops as it’s way too overwhelming. Unfortunately I learned the hard way.
I would definitely make this again. Great flavors and the integrity of the scallops is preserved.
Good recipe with lots of flavor.....but I had to cut the Garlic Salt in half and substitute.
The instructions on how to cook the scallops was perfect!!
Outstanding!

After reading a few other reviews first, I used garlic powder, no salt and added a pinch of curry powder just for fun. It was pretty good. I expected the horseradish to go better with the curry, but like I said, it was just a tiny bit. I really like the idea of the flavor combination though and I will definitely try it again. Plus, now my apartment smells like bacon!
Delish! Yummy perfection... Perfect as is :)
Awesome!
